objective: Publish one machine-generated phase-gate status for incremental multi-scenario delivery: for each of the four release phases, record its required issues, entry and exit criteria, the committed artifact each member issue produced, whether that gate currently proves itself, the evidence class the phase reaches, rollback/hold status and the owner sign-off it needs, so release notes can link a generated phase table instead of a hand-written claim that partial work is a physical capability.
decision_supported: Whether a release can point at one generated artifact that states which multi-scenario phase is actually complete, which gate is still unproven, and what evidence class each phase reaches, instead of a hand-written roadmap that could present a blocked or scripted-only phase as a finished physical capability.
acceptance: the phase status lists the four delivery phases with their required issues, entry criteria, exit criteria and required evidence classes, derived from one committed table rather than retyped per surface

each phase is marked complete only when every member gate currently proves itself and the readiness report marks every registered identity software ready; a phase with a missing or failing gate is never rendered as complete, and the gate fails when the committed artifact disagrees with a regeneration

phase status separates software readiness from scripted, Gazebo and physical validation: a software-complete phase records gazebo and physical as unproven while release_eligible stays false, so partial work is never presented as a physical capability

the machine-readable artifact records the commit, the configuration hash over its inputs and the volatile fields, and states that a test outcome, a gate verdict or an eligibility flag may not be hand-edited
release notes, the generated page and both READMEs are rendered from the same committed data, and the gate recomputes them so a published table cannot disagree with the artifact
every phase records the owner sign-off it needs, and a phase that requires a human approval records that the approval is outstanding rather than implied by a passing gate
evidence: docs/releases/phase-status-v1.json records a PASS or FAIL verdict per phase gate with the artifact it read
tools/scripts/check_phase_gates.py exits 0 PASS / 1 FAIL / 2 INCOMPLETE and prints the phase finding it refuses
tests/unit/test_phase_gates.py drives a phase-complete-with-a-missing-gate refusal as well as a success
docs/releases/phase-gates.md and the README blocks are the output of the same generation, so the gate compares bytes rather than trusting a typed table
stop_conditions: stop if a required gate cannot be evaluated read-only, and record the phase as unproven rather than assuming it passed
stop and report rather than invent a phase status when the readiness report is missing or stale
stop if the change would need to modify interfaces/, libs/contracts/ or any hardware path; that requires a separate Issue and human approval
stop if a phase can only be called complete by weakening an existing gate
risks_and_fallbacks: a phase could be marked complete from a stale gate result; fallback is that the gate recomputes each phase from its live probe and fails a committed artifact that disagrees
a phase could overclaim an evidence class; fallback is that gazebo and physical are copied from the readiness report and a test asserts they stay false while no real run backs them
the configuration hash could be unstable across machines; fallback is that it hashes canonical sorted JSON of named inputs and a test asserts two generations in one checkout agree
release notes could drift from the artifact; fallback is that the page, the release-notes block and both README blocks are generated from the same committed JSON and compared by the gate
rollback is a revert of this commit; the status, the gate and the generated tables are additive and no registry, manifest, seed or runtime path changes
